title: Durable Assimilation Record Persistence Foundation
objective: Establish the authoritative durable persistence boundary for records produced by the existing deterministic Assimilation pipeline so generated extraction, segment, classification, transformation, and derived-object records can survive process memory while preserving existing identifiers, provenance, deterministic pipeline behavior, raw-source immutability, and subsystem authority boundaries.
architecturalContext: The production Assimilation pipeline already performs deterministic extraction, segmentation, classification, and derivation.
Filesystem ingestion already durably preserves immutable raw source bytes and source-asset storage references.
Generated Assimilation records currently remain in memory after pipeline completion despite architecture and ADR contracts describing them as durable records.
The existing Knowledge bridge consumes Assimilation records in memory, but Knowledge persistence and production Knowledge handoff are separate concerns and are excluded from this objective.

River Development Agent persistence systems establish the architectural convention of keeping persistence behind explicit boundaries rather than embedding storage authority into deterministic engines.
acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated Assimilation persistence boundary durably stores generated extraction, segment, classification, transformation, and derived-object records produced by a successful production Assimilation run.
Persistence preserves the existing record identifiers and complete serialized record data without reconstructing or replacing deterministic pipeline outputs.
Persisted generated records are separated from immutable raw-source storage and do not modify, overwrite, or reinterpret source bytes or source-asset provenance.

Production Assimilation composes persistence after successful deterministic assimilation rather than granting persistence authority to extraction, segmentation, classification, derivation, or pipeline engines.
A failed Assimilation pipeline does not persist a misleading complete generated-record set.
Equivalent successful Assimilation results persist deterministically except for filesystem/environmental location details that are explicitly outside record identity.
The persistence boundary rejects unsafe record paths or identifier-derived traversal rather than allowing records to escape the configured persistence root.
Existing production Assimilation callers remain compatible unless an additive return value is required and proven necessary.
Knowledge persistence, Knowledge Engine mutation, production Knowledge handoff, databases, remote object storage, model invocation, network access, commit, push, and deployment are not introduced.

Tests prove durable round-trip storage, identifier preservation, raw-source separation, traversal safety, successful production integration, failure behavior, and existing Assimilation regression compatibility.
approvalBoundaries: Do not modify raw-source ingestion or immutable source storage.
Do not add Knowledge persistence or production Knowledge handoff.
Do not introduce database, remote storage, network, model, credential, execution-authorization, commit, or publication authority.
Approved scope amendment: pipeline/engine.ts and pipeline/types.ts may change only to additively expose the authoritative TransformationRecord produced for derivation to production composition.
Do not otherwise redesign deterministic extraction, segmentation, classification, derivation, or pipeline behavior.
No further scope expansion is authorized.
commitMessage: ASSIMILATION-001: Build durable assimilation record persistence foundation
